methods.label: Count colorings along rotation loops
methods.explanation:
A position ends white exactly when its original square was white and the square rotating into that position was also white. This lets us count successful original colorings.

The center rotates to itself, so it must originally be black. The four corners rotate among themselves in a loop, and the four edge-middle squares form a separate loop.

Consider either four-position loop, listing its positions in clockwise rotation order. A white square moves into the next position. Thus two consecutive positions in this order cannot both originally be white, since one would remain white after the rotation and repainting.

Count the allowed colorings by their number of white positions. There is \(1\) coloring with no whites and \(4\) with one white. With two whites, they must occupy opposite positions, giving \(2\) colorings. Three or four whites necessarily include consecutive white positions, so there are no further possibilities. Each loop therefore has
\[
1+4+2=7
\]
allowed colorings.

The center, corners, and edge-middle positions are disjoint and together specify the entire original grid. Every choice of an allowed coloring for each loop works, so there are \(1\cdot7\cdot7=49\) successful grids, with none counted twice.

The \(9\) independent fair color choices produce \(2^9=512\) equally likely original grids. Hence the probability is
\[
\boxed{\frac{49}{512}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution uses quarter-turn correspondences, small exhaustive coloring cases, and favorable outcomes divided by equally likely outcomes.

candidate.annotationRationale: The targets are a finite equally likely probability calculation and counting colorings under the local restriction induced by rotation. Rotation correspondence supports identifying the loops, and multiplication combines their choices. Adjacency here means consecutive positions under rotation, so no ordinary shared-side coloring restriction is imposed.

review.mathematicalCheck: A final white position requires both its original color and its incoming color to be white. Thus the center must be black, and each four-position rotation loop must avoid consecutive whites. Each loop has exactly \(1+4+2=7\) valid colorings, giving \(7^2/2^9=49/512\) without omissions or duplication.
